items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: he knew me but I didn't know him

ctx.x: I remember Juaro, Manuel Perez. I used to like to hear them men play trumpet because it takes three trumpet players to play them fumes and parades. And them too used to play the parade, you see. And both of them was loud and they could play. You see them. Joe Oliver and Manuel Perez. Now Freddie Carford, I heard him a couple of times but I don't know, he just got on out of my sight. I didn't, I never was around no place where he was playing regular. He went on away.
Did you hear Bunk Johnson? Was he here in those days?

Well, nah. Bunk, he was, he was, he was here a while and then he moved on up to, up to country somewhere. But he wasn't playing, he knew me but I didn't know him. He was playing, he was playing dances around there but I didn't know, I didn't know him. When he come here with George Lewis, he knew me right at the corner where I stood. But I didn't know him.

items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: And the Mississippi River man was boiling. Like he was angry.

ctx.x: Yeah. Then I had been coming up here. I had an auntie waking up on St. Charles Street, right St. Charles and Louisiana Avenue for a man from down the country down there. Well, I stayed up there with her a while before the storm. You know what I mean? I'd come and go, come and go. But I was in the country when that storm came up. And I was laying down in the bed and that 1915 storm came up. And when I seen that house on joint like that, I said, it's time for me to go. Fell apart up the rafters, huh? Yes. I mean,…
That was down, way down below Violet. Is it farther than Pointe?
